title: Show HN: Nodecode, open-source living agent in Lisp that rewrites itself for you
summary: Hi HN, we're Mike and Thom. Agents of the future should only have one tool (the interpreter, ideally a LISP eval), nothing more or less; to interact with the world. Agents remember by writing markdown files. NODECODE remembers by rewriting itself. And that is in itself a new paradigm in working with agents. What if memories, skills, MCPs, provider connectors, tools, etc. all live under the same image as *.lisp files instead of in disarray across random folders? Ask it for something it can’t do, and it writes what it needs into its OWN running image and keeps it even after a restart. (Changes in a LISP image have significantly lower ceremony and overhead than in harnesses written in other languages): Small intuitive scenario: > you can't read PDFs. teach yourself. (defun read-pdf (path) ...) ; runs at once, kept (read-pdf "invoices/0421.pdf") ;; Globex owes $1,240.00, due Oct 24, unpaid. [… rest of PDF content] read-pdf is still there after a restart, in your terminal, and in every other UI clients (Discord, web app, etc.) Technically at a lower level; NODECODE runs as one process in SBCL, a Common Lisp system, and shells attach to it. The model has one tool: it evaluates LISP in the running program. Code is data, so a program can rewrite itself while it runs. What the model defines runs at once and is kept, one file per definition, committed with git, loaded at every start. Why LISP now? Current SOTA models have reached an optimum point in how they efficiently work with LISP, though not as fluently as Python. Still, we believe AGI will understand ANY language (past/present/future) by understanding the crux of any given language, and not through excessive and expensive pretraining scheme. Why LISP in general? We believe LISP is the current language that communicates to the world with the least bandwidth. Why another LISP agent? The LISP harnesses we found are hard to use unless you already know the language itself, and so we had this idea of simplifying and condensing the UX to be user friendly for the masses, while leveraging the power of LISP. Code as data is what lets an agent change itself, and that shouldn't need a LISP hacker to run. NODECODE is our first step toward putting it on everyone's PC and mobile. You ask in plain words, the model writes LISP, and you get briefed in natural language; that is how it should be. Extensions? Code as data also suits extensions. We see NODECODE as a living agent organism. To us, it feels very much alive, and so this brings us to the Cells system. A Cell is a folder that teaches NODECODE something new: a chat room it can live in (e.g Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc. - Yes we made Cells for channels to have it act as a very capable personal agent), a skill, a memory, MCPs, new tools, etc. Install one from our Cell hub or ask it to write a custom, personalized one. Either way it is more code the agent can read and change. Your terminal, a browser tab, your phone and bots in Discord, Telegram and Slack all attach to that SAME gateway process, so a tool it writes in one is there in ALL of them. Over time it becomes yours and it is continuously evolving; the organism within it; NODECODE. MIT License. https://github.com/nodecode-ai/nodecode X/twitter/demo launch post: https://x.com/pomterree/status/2113721985167728757 docs: https://nodecode.ai/docs

title: Local-first video production workspace for people and AI agents
story_key: story|variant:video|title:local first video production workspace for people and ai agents
content_excerpt: Local-first video production workspace for people and AI agents, by TriHerm Labs / Fernando Abishai. Cutmark is a local-first video production workspace for people and AI agents, built by TriHerm Labs and created by Fernando Abishai. Record talking-head video, keep the source files on your Mac, and work with the AI agent you already use on scripts, storyboards, edits, review notes, thumbnails, and post drafts. Cutmark supports Claude Code, Codex, pi, and opencode in its in-app chat, and exposes the same local production workspace through MCP for compatible clients. The first-run setup can guide you through missing dependencies. No AI provider is installed until you choose one and press Install . Download Cutmark.dmg from the latest GitHub release, open it, and copy Cutmark.app to Applications. Cutmark 0.3.0 uses an explicitly authorized ad-hoc signing channel, like 0.2.0, and is not notarized . On first launch, macOS may require System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway . The repository retains a separate, protected Developer ID + Apple notarization path for production-signed releases once Apple credentials are configured. The macOS application is a Swift/SwiftUI package in Sources/Cutmark , with tests in Tests/CutmarkTests . The distributed application is Cutmark.app with bundle identifier com.triherm.cutmark . Projects contain sessions. Sessions contain scripts, recordings, edits, storyboards, thumbnails, post files, and metadata. You can change the library folder from the app. Cutmark does not require a hosted project database for this workflow. The packaged Cutmark MCP server is local-first and can be connected to compatible agent clients on the same Mac. For ChatGPT, a private Mac can use OpenAI's Secure MCP Tunnel to launch the local stdio server. See docs/chatgpt-mcp.md . Do not expose the loopback server directly to the public internet. A public deployment needs a stable HTTPS endpoint and appropriate authentication and per-user isolation. CI runs the Python MCP suite and Swift tests on macOS. Tags matching v* reuse the successful CI result for the same commit, then build Cutmark.app , package Cutmark.dmg , verify the artifact, and create a GitHub Release. Create the tag after CI on main is green; an early tag fails quickly and can be re-run after CI finishes. The protected production workflow uses the production-release GitHub environment with the Apple Developer ID and notarization credentials described in docs/releasing.md . Production

title: Show HN: God – real-time control room for LLM agent societies (EMNLP 2026 demo)
story_key: story|title:god real time control room for llm agent societies emnlp 2026 demo
content_excerpt: 🌩️ Be like a god to a town of agents. Pause time. Whisper to a soul. Bend the next step. Reset the world — all from a single click. 🌐 Live Demo · 🚀 Quick Start · Updates · Roadmap · Highlights · Features · Built-in Experiments · Public Site · AtomGit Mirror · Developer Docs · Contributing · 🌏 中文 Most agent-society demos let you watch a simulation play out. GOD gives you the controls. Replay a run, question any resident, change what happens next, and export a pack others can rerun, all from one screen. It is built for inspecting language-agent societies, not for claiming they are socially realistic. Live control room: PKU map, step controls, targeted ask, and resident roster in one view. Browse everything in your browser on the public site : curated replays, map packs, agent packs, and downloadable experiments. No install or API key needed. Left to right: the public site homepage, downloadable map packs, and downloadable agent packs. On the first run the script installs everything, opens a browser-based setup wizard , and waits for you to finish. You never have to edit .env or pass command-line flags by hand. The Setup Wizard: model config, experiment choice, and custom society creation in one browser flow. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. When the wizard hands off, the script prints a URL like: GOD is intentionally local-first: the control room, backend, runtime bridge, experiment files, and replay store all run on your machine. The model endpoint is the only external service you choose. GOD ships two built-in experiments and treats them exactly like experiments you publish yourself. The setup wizard writes the selected experiment to .god/current_experiment.json ; start , open , and new-run then act only on that current experiment. More downloadable scenarios live on the public site : Empty City Gate, Gaokao Blackout, Hogwarts Parent Meeting, and others. .env is intentionally local-only and only stores model, API, port, and similar machine settings. It no longer decides the default experiment or map, so an old GOD_MAP_ID=pku cannot make GOD Town load the PKU map. A late-spring Tuesday morning at 8:20. Sunny, 18°C, light breeze. A 200-person town with 10 residents who know each other but don't live in each other's pockets . It is a slice-of-life simulation, not a quest script. ➡️ Choose god_town in the Setup Wizard to make this the current experiment. It is bound to hypothesis_god_town/experiment_1 and the the_ville map. ➡️ See hypothesis_god_town/expe

title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves
summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.

title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
summary: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.

title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
summary: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.

title: claude-code v2.1.309
summary:
What's changed

  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
  • Fixed macOS sandbox denyWrite glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with --mcp-config
  • Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions
  • Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open
  • Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the cd is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain cd
  • Fixed an Edit(path) deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
  • Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
  • Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
  • Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from ! mode
  • Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
  • Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that jq could not parse
  • Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's /proc
  • Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed
  • Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization
  • Fixed the claude remote-control status line showing HEAD as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository
  • Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and --tools rules given on the leader's command line
  • Fixed sessions renamed with /rename appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive --resume
  • Fixed the /rewind list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through /code-review --fix, a subagent or a shell command
  • Fixed /privacy-settings showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched
  • Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug
  • Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript
  • Fixed a skill in an --add-dir folder being unreachable when another skill already held its name; it is now offered as <folder>:<name>
  • Fixed /verify and /code-review not finding a nested package's own skill when its files were changed from the shell
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that ant beta:worker poll --on-work passes trace context to the command
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill's C# tracing setup missing spans from the cloud platform clients
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that API spans for requests to Claude Platform on AWS can't join the caller's trace
  • Fixed hooks that run in PowerShell not blocking when the hook's program exits with code 2, and on Windows PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks with "shell": "powershell" failing open when Git for Windows isn't installed
  • Fixed a mod's turn.step hook that names a model by alias, such as haiku, failing every request with a model error: the alias now resolves to its model
  • Fixed plugins and skills synced from claude.ai being removed, sometimes mid-session, after a disk read error
  • Fixed artifact publishes and updates being refused for some ordinary pages, such as pages with certain minified scripts or artifacts Claude could not read first
  • Fixed Claude asking for permission on each artifact update for the rest of a turn after the conversation was compacted in that turn
  • Fixed fine-grained tool streaming staying off on Amazon Bedrock when ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL is set to the default bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com endpoint
  • Fixed the "Waiting for API response" hint flickering behind gateways that send only keepalive pings: routes off Anthropic's backend now wait 45 seconds
  • Fixed Claude notifying unrelated GitHub users by writing role names and placeholders as mentions in PRs, issues and comments
  • Linux: Fixed sandbox write denies lifting when a background command outlived the session
  • Windows: Fixed PowerShell permission checks auto-approving some Set-Location or cd commands that target the current directory and carry extra arguments; these now prompt for approval
  • macOS: Fixed the "Install Command Line Developer Tools" dialog opening each time Claude Code starts on a Mac without Xcode or the Command Line Tools
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed --startup-timeout-min stopping a session whose first prompt, such as /code-review, was still working in a subagent; a frozen process is still stopped
  • Improved the speed of many git commands Claude Code runs for itself on Windows; on every platform, errors from those commands now show in English even when git is set to another language
  • Improved the error when a hooks module is nested too deep to load: it now names the file instead of showing a bare stack-overflow message
  • Improved disk-full handling: a Bash command cut off by a full disk now says so and names the folder to free up, and starting on a full temp volume prints a clear message, not a raw ENOSPC error
  • Improved the /claude-api skill to offer API tracing alongside SDK tracing when asked to add OpenTelemetry
  • Improved the /claude-api skill to check the live docs before saying a feature is unsupported
  • Self-hosted runner: Improved sessions that move to a new runner: Claude now sees the tool call that was interrupted, marked as outcome unknown
  • Updated the bundled dataviz skill to accept APCA as a text-contrast measure (keeping WCAG 2 ratios where AA conformance is required), add an apca(text, background) function to its palette validator scripts, and say whether a label inside a colored chart fill should be white or near-black
  • Updated the /claude-api skill: service account keys and Workload Identity Federation tokens can now manage OpenTelemetry destinations
  • Changed sed -i to get the standard Bash prompt and run as written, not a simulated file-edit preview; like other Bash edits, it is no longer restored by /rewind
  • Changed claude ultrareview to require workspace trust: it asks on a terminal, else refuses; scripts pass --trust-workspace, which takes no value (put a PR number or base branch before it), or set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRAREVIEW_TRUST_CHECK=1
  • Changed the dangerous rm and rmdir prompt in bypass permissions mode in the Desktop app and VS Code to deny the command at once with a rewrite hint, so unattended sessions keep going
  • Changed commands the settings exclude from the sandbox to ask before writing to its write-list paths while the sandbox is enabled but cannot run; the unsandboxed fallback is refused there
  • Changed worktree creation and reuse so git no longer fetches objects on demand, in ordinary clones and in partial clones with a Bash sandbox configured; such a partial clone fetches them first
  • Changed the /claude-api skill to build Managed Agents subagent teams on multiagent_20261001 with dynamic workflows on by default, instead of coordinator
  • [VSCode] Added a log warning that says what to do when dictation or the extension's own requests fail certificate verification, such as behind a TLS-inspecting proxy
  • [VSCode] Fixed the Claude panel staying blank after the editor cached an incomplete copy of its files; it now recovers by itself, or says what went wrong and how to fix it
  • [VSCode] Fixed Session history filling up with empty "Untitled" sessions each time you start a new session without sending a message
  • [VSCode] Fixed long slash-command messages such as /goal filling the chat panel; they now fold behind Show more like other prompts (#97469)
  • [VSCode] Fixed long messages not folding behind Show more after the chat panel is made narrower
  • [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+J in the chat input always inserting a newline: it is now left to VS Code and the OS when "ctrl+j" is set to null in the Chat context of ~/.claude/keybindings.json
  • [VSCode] Fixed a mod's "From the … plugin" label above the prompt being drawn over the slash command and @-mention menus (#102981)
  • [VSCode] Fixed an empty list item, paragraph or code block, and list items renumbered from 1, when pasting copied LaTeX math
  • [VSCode] Fixed the feedback error showing only an HTTP status when your organization does not accept feedback
  • [VSCode] Improved Edit and Write speed in the chat panel: the wait for new problems after each edit is now 0.75 seconds in most cases, down from 1 to 1.5 seconds
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the Add connector list in routine forms saying no connectors were available while they were still loading
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the cloud environment editor shuffling environment variables and adding backslashes to values that contain both kinds of quote
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the self-hosted environment details dialog in admin settings so its title, tabs and buttons stay in view while only the content scrolls
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the "read documentation" tool row in cloud sessions, which showed escaped JSON instead of a readable page
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved a cloud session's Changes pane, which now says when it lists only pushed commits or only Claude's edits
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack posting a draft you approved for a channel into your DM by mistake; a post with no channel is now refused so it can go to the approved channel
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Allow and Deny on Claude's approval cards in Slack doing nothing when the session had stopped; your answer now restarts the session
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude ignoring untagged messages in a Slack channel after its workspace moved to a different Claude organization, including unshared channels on Enterprise Grid
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in a Slack channel posting a threaded reply before reading a newer message someone had just added to that thread
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed the Slack page in Claude Tag admin settings saying no workspaces were connected when the list failed to load; it now shows an error with a Retry button

title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents
summary: LLM agents need long-term memory that can recover precise and mutually consistent evidence from growing interaction histories, particularly when answers depend on relations among facts rather than isolated semantic matches. Current memory pipelines remain vulnerable at two stages: indexing errors can fragment repeated entities or merge distinct ones, and online retrieval often treats initial similarity scores as final even when the surrounding graph provides evidence for revising them. We introduce ActionRAG, a graph memory architecture that couples cautious indexing with query-time graph retroevaluation. Its indexing pipeline reconciles type labels and applies tiered entity resolution. Given a query, dual-channel entity and triple retrieval forms an initial evidence set and induces a bounded local graph. Query-conditioned receiver-normalized diffusion refines triple scores using local path structure. Seed protection, hub-penalized flux, and triple materialization preserve direct evidence while recovering missed connections. We evaluate ActionRAG on MemoryAgentBench (MAB), which tests accurate retrieval, conflict resolution, long-range understanding, and test-time learning. Across its eight deterministic-scoring columns, ActionRAG achieves 55.1 average accuracy, improving over the strongest retrieval-based memory baseline by 5.4 points. Under MAB's query-time cost accounting, mean synthesis cost stays below \$0.001 per query on the four reported cost columns, and the sum of separately measured retrieval-side p99 components is 440.7 ms on our consumer Apple Silicon setup.

title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
summary: Despite advances in multilingual text representations, effective dense retrieval for Persian remains constrained by the limited availability of language-specific training resources and compact embedding models. We present Yalda Embedding, a 595.8-million-parameter Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using more than one million query-document pairs. On eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB, the model achieves the highest macro-average among the evaluated 0.6B models, scoring 0.5488 and outperforming Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and F2LLM-v2-0.6B on every task. It also approaches Qwen3-Embedding-4B, winning on four tasks, tying on one, and trailing by 0.0075 in macro-average. An incremental ablation study examines contrastive batch size, optimization stabilization, and relational knowledge distillation from F2LLM-v2-8B. Under the one-epoch training setup, contrastive fine-tuning alone yields a modest mean improvement over initialization and regressions on two tasks. The final distilled configuration improves all eight tasks over the non-distilled model, raising the mean from 0.4813 to 0.5488 without increasing inference-time model size. These gains include hard-negative evaluation tasks despite training without explicitly mined or supplied hard negatives. We release model weights, training and evaluation code, the pairwise dataset, and its teacher-embedded counterpart, enabling inspection of data composition and training procedures, independent evaluation, and reuse without repeating expensive teacher inference.
